newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia debt futures firm despite wages warning.
newsitem.headline: Australia debt futures firm despite wages warning.

text.p: Australian bond and bill futures extended their early rally despite Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane saying prospects for improving inflation had been set back by recent data on wages growth.
June 10-year bond futures touched a high of 92.330 compared with 92.280 just before the lunchtime recess, while June bills firmed to 94.06 from 94.03.
Macfarlane, who had been addressing the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce, said that the RBA may lift rates or forego rate cuts if it sees further bad news on wages and prices.
However, he also said: "if we get good news and our assessment is for lower growth in wages and prices, we can, other things equal, let the economy run faster," he said.
"This may be done by reducing interest rates or, depending on the cicumstances, refraining from raising them."

The market got off to a firm start to the session after a particularly benign U.S. PPI report on Wednesday, which is seen lessening the chances of a Fed tightening on May 20, and the advance was extended when bill futures perked up on U.S. buying.
